tagline: 444 miles at fifty, on the Kaintucks' long walk home.
intro: Out of Natchez the parkway sets off northeast, two lanes with no commercial traffic and a speed limit of 50 for most of the way, bound for Pasquo outside Nashville by way of Jackson, Tupelo and the northwest corner of Alabama. Its gentle curves keep mostly to the high ground of the ridges, close to the old foot trail and the game traces under it.

The Kaintucks made the trail famous. Flatboatmen floated goods down to Natchez, and since the river was too strong to go home on, about 10,000 of them walked or rode back up the Trace in 1810, sleeping on the floors of inns called stands. Meriwether Lewis died at one of them in 1809.

moments.title: Emerald Mound
moments.text: Eight acres of flat-topped earthwork, 35 feet high, built up around a natural hill between 1250 and 1600 and later the Natchez people's main ceremonial center.

moments.title: Colbert Ferry
moments.text: The Chickasaw George Colbert ran the Tennessee River ferry here from 1800 to 1819, and during the Creek War he was paid $150 for carrying 600 men and horses across.

moments.title: Double Arch Bridge
moments.text: Near the north end the road crosses Birdsong Hollow 145 feet up, on concrete arches that carry the deck with no spandrel columns, the weight gathered at the crown.
